status: DESCRIPTIVE — CAP-80 LARGER-28 OVERLAP DECOMPOSITION; NO TARGET, FREEZE, GRANT OR A1 CELL
question: At loop cap 120 / prediction cap 80, does K coverage explain the two larger-28 joint C1 failures?
definition: Per-seed A, K, A∩K, A\K and K\A on the six larger-28 candidate streams at prediction cap 80, with C1 floor 60.  A\K is the predicted-not-carried overlap loss; K\A is the carried-not-predicted pool.
method: One no-arm replay per seed at cap 80.  A, K and A∩K must reproduce the committed prediction-cap rows exactly.  Every candidate edge's A and K membership is recorded so the overlap is decomposed by seed, family and support.
reading: All six larger-28 seeds clear A marginally (A 75-91), so the two joint failures are not A shortages.  At cap 80, K covers 56/75 and 51/83 of the A edges on seeds 20660102 and 20660103, leaving 19 and 32 A edges uncarried; only 4 and 9 of those need to be covered to reach 60.  K volume is not scarce (K 124 and 105 against A 75 and 83), so the failure is selective K coverage: the joint ceiling loses 19 and 32 rows to A\K.
not_evidence: A descriptive overlap decomposition on six no-arm larger-28 seeds at one cap pair.  It measures A\K and K\A availability; it is not a treatment, a K-repair result, target viability or a successor.  Full K coverage is a counterfactual, not an engine change.
